Air Force Falcons.status: Returning starter — the first time in four years Calhoun has one.
Air Force Falcons.career_experience: Established starter; the guide rates him the best quarterback Air Force has had in years.
Air Force Falcons.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Air Force Falcons.passing: Not addressed in guide individually. Team-level: Air Force averaged 29.8 points and 407 yards per game.
Air Force Falcons.rushing: Led the team in rushing, with Owen Allen second behind him.
Air Force Falcons.efficiency: Team-level: 11th nationally in EPA per play and 15th in both rushing EPA per play and rushing success rate.
Air Force Falcons.competition: None described — Szarka is the settled starter.
Air Force Falcons.author_confidence: High. The guide rates him the best quarterback Air Force has had in years and says Calhoun now has what he needs.
Air Force Falcons.positive_case: An experienced quarterback returning to one of the country's most efficient offenses, with a strong offensive line, and no expectations attached — attention is on UNLV, New Mexico and North Dakota State instead.
Air Force Falcons.concerns: Not addressed as a quarterback concern; the guide's stated hinge is the defense.
Air Force Falcons.scheme_fit: Established — the option offense he already runs, under Troy Calhoun.
Air Force Falcons.supporting_cast: Owen Allen returns as last season's second-leading rusher. Only four starters return overall and three offensive line starters departed, though the guide notes the unit's career starts match last season's.
Air Force Falcons.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, and the guide names the hinge precisely — the defense. Creeping back toward merely average would make Air Force a true Mountain West threat. Schedule shape favors them: North Dakota State and UNLV travel to Colorado, Hawaii is avoided entirely, and it sees a possible surprise appearance in the Mountain West Championship, something that has not happened since 2015.
Air Force Falcons.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The quarterback is treated as a settled strength; the guide's stated hinge is defensive improvement.

Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.career_experience: Established starter; named preseason Offensive Player of the Year.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide notes an ankle injury eventually cost him starts against Sam Houston State and Portland State.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.passing: 66% completions for 3,106 yards with 24 touchdowns to nine interceptions.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.rushing: Not a dual threat in high school, but he showed he could escape pressure and use his legs; he rushed for 614 yards and six touchdowns over his final two seasons at Bishop Gorman.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.competition: None described — Alejado is the settled starter.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.author_confidence: High. The guide says he has given no reason to doubt his growth and names him preseason Offensive Player of the Year.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.positive_case: An incredible 2025 produced despite a nagging ankle injury suffered in the opener against Stanford, with a plethora of weapons available and Pofele Ashlock on the preseason all-conference team.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.concerns: The ankle. The guide poses the real question as whether a healthy ankle lets him add a running dimension.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.supporting_cast: Strong — a plethora of weapons, headlined by preseason all-conference Pofele Ashlock.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 7.5 wins, hinging on Alejado's growth. The guide goes further than the win total, calling Hawaii a solid bet to be Mountain West champion, and highlights the structural advantage that Hawaii hosts all three teams ahead of it in the market — UNLV, North Dakota State and New Mexico. It reports Hawaii as the fourth choice at DraftKings at +450.
Hawaii Rainbow Warriors.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide states the Over hinges on Alejado's growth.

Nevada Wolf Pack.status: Transfer — from UCLA; expected to win an open three-way competition rather than confirmed.
Nevada Wolf Pack.career_experience: 6-foot-6 and started on the road at Ohio State.
Nevada Wolf Pack.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a count.
Nevada Wolf Pack.passing: Not addressed in guide for Duncan. Incumbent Carter Jones returns with 1,019 yards, six touchdowns and eight interceptions.
Nevada Wolf Pack.efficiency: Team-level: 114th in passing success rate, 133rd in passing EPA per play and in the 34th percentile in explosive pass rate.
Nevada Wolf Pack.turnovers: Not addressed in guide for Duncan; Carter Jones threw eight interceptions against six touchdowns.
Nevada Wolf Pack.competition: A genuine three-way race. The guide records that Choate insists the race is tight going into camp, while expecting Duncan to win eventually.
Nevada Wolf Pack.backup: Incumbent Carter Jones and three-year Reno stalwart AJ Bianco.
Nevada Wolf Pack.author_confidence: Moderate. The guide judges Duncan showed enough in his Hawaii starts to expect he wins the job and performs admirably, while concluding that whoever wins, Nevada needs far more from the position.
Nevada Wolf Pack.positive_case: Duncan is 6-foot-6 with a start at Ohio State behind him, and the guide expects a steadier hand at the position to unlock enough offensive talent to be much more effective.
Nevada Wolf Pack.concerns: One of the country's least efficient passing attacks last season, and a race the head coach says is still tight.
Nevada Wolf Pack.supporting_cast: Improving. Leading rusher Caleb Ramseur is gone but Herschel Turner returns after 395 yards at 5.1 per carry, behind a line that looks strong on paper with three starters back including preseason all-conference left tackle Jack Foster and right tackle Zach Cochnauer. Choate added Jacob Norcross and Ethan Newman Jr from Memphis at center and right guard.
Nevada Wolf Pack.portal_context: Duncan from UCLA; Norcross and Newman from Memphis.
Nevada Wolf Pack.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins. Quarterback is an obvious question, but the guide judges Duncan showed enough to expect he wins the job and performs admirably. The schedule is hard — road games at North Dakota State and UNLV plus home games with Air Force, New Mexico and Hawaii — but the guide concludes the defense's potential under Choate plus offensive upside could produce an upstart season.
Nevada Wolf Pack.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's Over is built on a steadier hand at quarterback unlocking the offense.
Nevada Wolf Pack.conflicts: The guide expects Duncan to win while recording that the head coach insists the race is tight. Both are stated; neither is resolved.

New Mexico Lobos.status: Returning starter — but the guide argues he may not be a lock.
New Mexico Lobos.career_experience: Led New Mexico to nine wins and a bowl.
New Mexico Lobos.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
New Mexico Lobos.passing: 2,486 yards with 13 touchdowns to 10 interceptions at 7.6 yards per attempt.
New Mexico Lobos.efficiency: 7.6 yards per attempt — which the guide characterizes as good rather than great.
New Mexico Lobos.competition: Live and injury-shadowed. Layne missed spring camp recovering from surgery on a torn flexor tendon in his throwing elbow, and Oregon transfer Luke Moga reportedly made the most of his absence and dazzled the media in Albuquerque.
New Mexico Lobos.backup: Oregon transfer Luke Moga, a former three-star and strong athlete with enough upside for Oregon to have recruited him.
New Mexico Lobos.author_confidence: Guarded. The guide's conclusion is conditional: if Layne is not healthy or struggles early, this could be Moga's job before season's end.
New Mexico Lobos.positive_case: He led New Mexico to nine wins and a bowl, and returns among 12 starters alongside reigning Defensive Player of the Year Jaxton Eck.
New Mexico Lobos.concerns: Elbow surgery that cost him spring camp, and production the guide calls good rather than great.
New Mexico Lobos.supporting_cast: Twelve starters return overall; the guide does not itemise the offensive skill positions.
New Mexico Lobos.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins, with the guide openly noting the juice on Over 7.5 and Under 8.5 makes this a tough play. Its core evidence is the favorite-role record: New Mexico closed as an underdog in seven games, but in the six where it was favored it went 3-3 straight up and just 1-5 against the spread — and this season it will be favored in most contests. Its conclusion is that this is a good team whose damage last season came as an underdog and which now looks overvalued as a favorite.
New Mexico Lobos.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Under is argued from role change and favorite-role record rather than from quarterback risk, though it flags the position as not actually settled.

North Dakota State Bison.status: New starter — promoted from within after Cole Payton was drafted.
North Dakota State Bison.previous_school: Not applicable — in the programme since 2022.
North Dakota State Bison.career_experience: Appeared in 10 games and has been in the system since 2022, so the guide says there should be no learning curve.
North Dakota State Bison.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records 10 appearances.
North Dakota State Bison.passing: 57% completions for 381 yards with four touchdowns and one interception.
North Dakota State Bison.turnovers: One interception against four touchdown passes.
North Dakota State Bison.competition: None described — Hayes is presented as the successor.
North Dakota State Bison.author_confidence: Neutral, framed through programme history rather than the player. The guide notes Cole Payton going to the Eagles at pick 178 marked the fifth Bison starting quarterback drafted in 11 years, and that Hayes now carries that pressure.
North Dakota State Bison.positive_case: Four years in the system with no learning curve, and a programme record of developing draftable quarterbacks.
North Dakota State Bison.concerns: The supporting cast: he takes over an offense missing its top two rushers and top two receivers.
North Dakota State Bison.scheme_fit: Established — he has been in the system since 2022.
North Dakota State Bison.supporting_cast: Depleted. The offense is missing its top two rushers and top two receivers, and North Dakota State lost two First-Team All-MVFC offensive linemen.
North Dakota State Bison.portal_context: North Dakota State took a different approach from most, signing 29 high school players and only nine transfers, of whom three played at Power Four programmes last season — one being punter Caleb McGrath. Just 10 starters return and zero portal starters were added.
North Dakota State Bison.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. The guide understands why NDSU is a short price to win the conference given its record, while judging expectations somewhat high: portal losses were immense with little brought back, and these are teams built with former Power Four players carrying real talent. Road games come at Air Force, UNLV, Hawaii and New Mexico — trips to every contender — and it answers its own question about winning most of those with a blunt doubtful.
North Dakota State Bison.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The guide's Under is argued from roster construction and schedule rather than from the quarterback, though it raises the position as a programme tradition now under test.

Northern Illinois Huskies.status: Transfer — from North Carolina, having previously been at Western Carolina; a mid-July addition.
Northern Illinois Huskies.career_experience: A one-time North Carolina commit and former Western Carolina quarterback who appeared in 18 games there.
Northern Illinois Huskies.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count; the guide records 18 appearances at Western Carolina.
Northern Illinois Huskies.passing: 271 of 365 for 3,508 yards with 38 touchdowns to two interceptions at Western Carolina; he set an NCAA record with 46 consecutive completions in a game against Wofford.
Northern Illinois Huskies.efficiency: 271 of 365 — and an NCAA record 46 consecutive completions in a single game.
Northern Illinois Huskies.competition: Effectively resolved by his arrival. Before it, Brady Davidson and Jalen Macon were the only returners, having combined to complete under 50% of their passes for four touchdowns and three interceptions.
Northern Illinois Huskies.author_confidence: Positive on the addition, negative on everything else. The guide calls his arrival a huge win while saying the vibes around the programme are not great.
Northern Illinois Huskies.positive_case: Exceptional Western Carolina production including an NCAA single-game record, arriving to replace a room that had completed under 50% of its passes.
Northern Illinois Huskies.concerns: The circumstances of his availability — released by the Tar Heels over academic issues in mid-July — and a team with no returning defensive starters, a new offense and a new conference.
Northern Illinois Huskies.scheme_fit: Not addressed in guide; the offense is new.
Northern Illinois Huskies.supporting_cast: Not addressed in guide in detail; roster turnover was immense, especially on defense.
Northern Illinois Huskies.portal_context: Dickens became suddenly available in the portal in mid-July after being released by North Carolina over academic issues, and Northern Illinois moved.
Northern Illinois Huskies.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 3.5 wins. The guide is unusually explicit about method here, saying data is always the best way to project but sometimes vibes matter — and the vibes are not great. Then the data: no returning starters on defense, a new offense and quarterback, and a new conference.
Northern Illinois Huskies.outlook_dependency: Moderate. The quarterback is the guide's one clearly positive development; its Under rests on the defense, the coaching situation and the conference move.

San Jose State Spartans.status: Transfer — from Hawaii; described as the presumed winner rather than a confirmed starter.
San Jose State Spartans.previous_school: Hawaii; worked his way up from Modesto Junior College.
San Jose State Spartans.career_experience: A seasoned and well-travelled redshirt senior; started two games at Hawaii in place of the injured Micah Alejado, winning both.
San Jose State Spartans.previous_starts: Two at Hawaii, against Sam Houston State and Portland State.
San Jose State Spartans.passing: 53 of 85 for 534 yards with five touchdowns and one interception in those two starts.
San Jose State Spartans.turnovers: One interception against five touchdown passes.
San Jose State Spartans.competition: The depth chart is completely new apart from one-time UCLA transfer Robert McDaniel, with Weaver the presumed winner.
San Jose State Spartans.author_confidence: Moderate and system-based. The guide judges Weaver likely gives San Jose State the best chance in this system.
San Jose State Spartans.positive_case: Two winning starts in place of an injured conference Offensive Player of the Year, and a profile the guide thinks suits coordinator Craig Stutzmann's Spread and Shred offense.
San Jose State Spartans.concerns: The offense that took the conference by storm two seasons ago fizzled in 2025, and the guide notes many opponents have now seen the tendencies.
San Jose State Spartans.scheme_fit: Central. The guide judges Weaver likely gives San Jose State the best chance specifically in Stutzmann's system.
San Jose State Spartans.supporting_cast: Severely depleted. The top five pass catchers are gone with four transfers making up the room; the guide names Anthony Ivey, a former four-star from Penn State, as the one to watch, handling it even-handedly — the step down is obviously massive and could be a red flag, but the pedigree is there and so is a system built to maximize him. It identifies a genuine pattern in Stutzmann's offense of a previously unheralded receiver erupting: Nick Nash produced 1,382 yards and 16 touchdowns in year one, and Danny Scudero caught 88 passes for 1,297 yards and 10 touchdowns last season.
San Jose State Spartans.portal_context: Per Phil Steele, San Jose State lost 24 starters to the portal and brought in two, with only three full-time starters returning from a three-win team.
San Jose State Spartans.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 4.5 wins. The guide entertains a repeat of 2023's seven-win surprise before explaining why the two ingredients — a surprising offense and a favorable schedule — are both absent, and closes with unusual candour about its own record, noting it was wrong about Niumatalolo in 2023 and is taking its chances saying he cannot do it again.
San Jose State Spartans.outlook_dependency: High. The guide's argument is that the offense's element of surprise has gone, which puts the burden on a new quarterback in a now-familiar system.

UNLV Rebels.status: Transfer — from Auburn; a one-time five-star, and the presumed starter.
UNLV Rebels.previous_starts: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
UNLV Rebels.competition: Not described as live, but the guide asks directly what happens if Arnold struggles and loses the job while Alex Orji is not the same athlete.
UNLV Rebels.backup: Former Michigan quarterback Alex Orji, coming off a catastrophic leg injury and not fully healthy in spring, whom the guide also describes as somewhat limited as a passer.
UNLV Rebels.author_confidence: Sceptical about sustainability rather than about Arnold specifically. The guide's logic is that UNLV cannot keep sustaining the quarterback success of the last three seasons, with this depth chart looking more flawed.
UNLV Rebels.positive_case: The precedent is drawn directly: Mullen took in Anthony Colandrea last season, made him Mountain West Offensive Player of the Year and sent him to Nebraska for a payday. UNLV has not returned a starting quarterback since Doug Brumfield in 2023, with five different starters over that span, yet still accumulated 30 wins and three title game appearances.
UNLV Rebels.concerns: A flawed depth chart, with Orji coming off a horrendous injury and limited as a passer, and the guide's stated doubt that the run of quarterback success can continue.
UNLV Rebels.scheme_fit: Dan Mullen's record of developing incoming portal quarterbacks is the stated mechanism.
UNLV Rebels.supporting_cast: Thin outside the backfield. Running back Jai'den Thomas is the known quantity, having run for 1,036 yards at 7.2 per carry with 13 total touchdowns, but beyond the first-team all-conference back there is little returning production, with all three top receivers gone; Taeshaun Lyons is the leading returnee at 13 receptions for 222 yards. Both running back depth and the receiver room consist of transfers expected to carry large loads.
UNLV Rebels.portal_context: Another roster built on transfers; Arnold from Auburn and Orji from Michigan are the quarterback additions.
UNLV Rebels.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 8.5 wins. Its logic is that UNLV cannot keep sustaining the quarterback success of the last three seasons, and it adds that it finds the staff's explanation for last season's defensive effort hard to buy. Its conclusion is that the schedule plus roster flaws make eight wins extremely likely — not that the team will be bad, but that nine-plus is a real challenge.
UNLV Rebels.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide states the co-favorite's season rests on Mullen working his magic at the position again.

UTEP Miners.status: Transfer — from Incarnate Word, having previously been at UCF; named the starter in May.
UTEP Miners.career_experience: Started a game and appeared in another for UCF in 2024, then a full season at Incarnate Word.
UTEP Miners.previous_starts: One at UCF, plus his Incarnate Word season.
UTEP Miners.passing: At UCF in 2024: 9 of 16 for 64 yards with an interception. At Incarnate Word last season: 70.9% for 2,142 yards with 16 touchdowns and four interceptions.
UTEP Miners.turnovers: Four interceptions against 16 touchdown passes at Incarnate Word; one interception in his brief UCF sample.
UTEP Miners.competition: Resolved — Scotty Walden named him the starter in May.
UTEP Miners.author_confidence: Cautiously positive. The guide says much depends on Colson, who has the upside, while framing the task as Herculean.
UTEP Miners.positive_case: A 70.9% completion rate with a 16-to-4 ratio and 287 rushing yards, named the starter in May.
UTEP Miners.concerns: The scale of the rebuild: turning around an offense that ranked 131st in EPA per play and 129th in success rate, while doing it without the top four rushers and top seven receivers. His UCF sample did not go well.
UTEP Miners.supporting_cast: Rebuilt from nothing. The baseline is poor — 116 rushing yards per game at 3.7 per carry, with the programme not averaging more than 3.9 since 2022. Walden added line help in left guard Brian Williams, an all-conference selection in the SWAC, and right tackle Jaymon Lamb, who played seven games for North Texas. At running back the guide names Missouri transfer Tavorus Jones the crown jewel, a former four-star who appeared in 20 games for the Tigers.
UTEP Miners.portal_context: Colson, Williams, Lamb and Jones all arrived through the portal; the guide says the staff has plugged holes decently.
UTEP Miners.betting_implications: Recommendation is Over 3.5 wins. There is enough on offense to be somewhat optimistic about climbing out of the national cellar, with much depending on Colson. The guide starts from the market — UTEP is the longest shot to win the Mountain West at DraftKings at 80-1 and carries the conference's lowest win total — and concludes there is a strong chance this is not the team that finishes last.
UTEP Miners.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide states much depends on Colson.

Wyoming Cowboys.status: Transfer — a former William & Mary recruit of coordinator Christian Taylor's, following him to Wyoming.
Wyoming Cowboys.previous_school: Not stated directly; the guide identifies him as one of Sawvel's former William & Mary recruits who already knows the system.
Wyoming Cowboys.career_experience: Not addressed in guide as a start count.
Wyoming Cowboys.passing: Totalled 3,000 passing and rushing yards with 31 touchdowns; the guide does not split passing out.
Wyoming Cowboys.rushing: Included in the 3,000 combined yards and 31 touchdowns; described as a dual threat.
Wyoming Cowboys.competition: None described — Hughes is presented as the addition that addresses the position.
Wyoming Cowboys.author_confidence: Positive and conditional. The guide says the needle clearly points up with Hughes adding a dynamic Wyoming has missed, while framing its number as a probability question.
Wyoming Cowboys.positive_case: A dual threat with 3,000 combined yards and 31 touchdowns who already knows the system, paired with a coordinator whose offenses generated explosive runs, used backs out of the backfield and led the country in passing efficiency.
Wyoming Cowboys.concerns: The baseline is dire — despite nine returning starters last season Wyoming averaged 16 points and 315 yards per game, ranking 128th nationally in EPA per play and 124th in success rate.
Wyoming Cowboys.scheme_fit: Maximal — Hughes was recruited by Christian Taylor at William & Mary and already knows the system.
Wyoming Cowboys.supporting_cast: Mixed. Leading rusher Samuel Harris returns as a sophomore behind a line with two starters and 41 career starts back. The top four receivers are gone, but the guide notes this is reportedly a strong tight end group, which matters in the new scheme.
Wyoming Cowboys.portal_context: Wyoming lost talent to the portal, but the guide cites Phil Steele that 77.2% of the roster is homegrown, meaning many players have been in the programme.
Wyoming Cowboys.betting_implications: Recommendation is Under 5.5 wins, with the upside case stated first: if Hughes and coordinator Christian Taylor are the match they look on paper, the offense could stun the conference and let Sawvel focus on a defense with a strong foundation. Its conclusion is framed as a probability question: this asks Wyoming to come out on the right side of 50-50 contests more often than not.
Wyoming Cowboys.outlook_dependency: Very high. The guide's entire upside case is the quarterback-coordinator pairing.
